14:3b. *Target-recalibrated estimator (added in rev 3):* the sources tell which items are harder; the target's own n answers tell how hard they are *for it*. Fit on the sample, by weighted least squares with weights 1/π, y_i ~ β0 + β1·s_i (+ β2·p̂_i^{CF}), where s_i is a source-only item score (logit of the source mean accuracy, or a low-rank/IRT item difficulty) and p̂_i^{CF} an optional cross-fitted model prediction; the estimate is the mean of the fitted values over all N items, i.e. the generalized-regression / PPI++ estimator with a **slope estimated from the target's own sample** instead of a λ tuned on source models. It needs no source-side tuning that mimics the evaluation split, which is where the tuned-λ difference estimator failed in extrapolation; its price is an O(1/n) bias and the variance of a 2–3 parameter fit at n≈10–100, both measured. This is the version of "bias by design, variance from sources" that does not need the target to resemble the sources.
15:3c. *Target-adaptive two-phase design (optional, Tier 2):* spend n/2 items on a stratified sample, fit the target's ability, then draw the other n/2 with π ∝ √(p̂_i(θ̂)(1−p̂_i(θ̂))) (floor ε), using the conditional inclusion probabilities of phase 2 in the estimator (valid conditional on phase 1). Aimed at the mismatch of source-average variance weights for a stronger target; unlike max-information CAT it stays a probability sample.
18:Factorial ablation (so a win cannot hide behind a weak comparator): design {uniform, stratified, uncertainty-proportional PPS (Active-Statistical-Inference style), balanced/source-matching, anchor medoids, IRT-CAT adaptive} × estimator {sample mean/Hájek, source-calibrated regression, model-based, difference with source-tuned λ, target-recalibrated regression (3b)}.
27:Tier 1 (cheap, all 13 benchmarks, must exist): (1) uniform random sample mean; (2) stratified random (strata by source difficulty / clusters); (3) source-calibrated regression (regress full score on subset score across sources, apply to target); (4) anchor points, k-medoids (Vivek et al.); (5) **balanced/source-matching selection** (choose or balance n items so the subset mean reproduces source models' full scores: greedy/herding/cube sampling/calibration weights) **with an overfitting check**: selected on sources, scored only on models excluded from selection and tuning; (6) ours, design + difference estimator, and design + target-recalibrated regression (3b).
14:- Related: sparse sample-level aggregation (ghosh2024onebench), efficient benchmarking by reducing items/configurations (perlitz-etal-2024-efficient).
20:- **Model-assisted survey estimation** (sarndal1992model): generalized regression/difference estimators use auxiliary predictions for variance reduction while staying design-unbiased.

input:
cd /hutian/wiki && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='Brief.md'
t=open(p).read()
old="This is the version of \"bias by design, variance from sources\" that does not need the target to resemble the sources."
assert old in t
new=old+"""

   *Lineage.* 3b is not a new estimator: it is the model-assisted generalized regression (GREG) estimator of survey sampling (Särndal, Swensson & Wretman 1992; `sarndal1992model`), and PPI++ with a slope fitted on the labelled sample (Angelopoulos et al. 2023). What the study adds is the application (source-model results as the covariate for a new model's score), the choice of s_i, and the controlled analysis of when it helps, above all for targets stronger than all sources.

   *Post-results status.* 3b was designed after results-v1 showed the failure of the source-tuned λ on the extrapolation targets; the paper says so. Its specification is fixed before the run: s_i ∈ {source-mean logit, rank-2 low-rank/IRT difficulty}, with or without p̂^{CF}, ridge (small fixed penalty on β1, β2, none on β0) or none; the grid is reported whole and one variant is chosen by the leave-one-benchmark-out rule of the Outline, not by the extrapolation targets. Evidence not tied to the design: 3b is also reported in the interpolation and lineage splits, where it was not motivated, and a cell not used in motivating it (extrapolation targets/draws not examined in results-v1, or the benchmark family held out by the rule) is flagged as the clean test.

   *Closest comparator.* "Stratify on source difficulty and post-stratify/regress" is the contrast that decides whether 3b adds anything: the (stratified design) × (3b with s_i = source difficulty) cell against (stratified) × (stratum-mean/Hájek) and (uniform) × (3b). The "about 10% or less over stratified" of results-v1 is the number this contrast settles; if 3b adds nothing over stratify-and-post-stratify, the paper reports that, and the contribution is the analysis and the robustness claim, not the estimator.

   *Small-n rule.* With n = 10–30 and a 0/1 outcome a 2–3 parameter linear fit can leave [0,1] or be unstable. Rule: fitted values are clipped to [0,1]; β is ridge-penalised; if the sample has fewer than 3 items of either class, or the weighted design matrix is rank-deficient, the estimator falls back to the Hájek sample mean. The fall-back rate by n and split is reported next to the error, and results at n where it exceeds 20% are marked as mostly the fall-back."""
t=t.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(t)
EOF
git add -A && git commit -qm "Brief rev 4: lineage, post-results status, closest comparator, small-n rule for 3b

shown.message:
I've covered all four points of the review in Brief rev 4 and closed `idea-repo`#5.

- **Post-results status:** §3b now says the estimator was designed after results-v1 showed the failure on the extrapolation targets. Its specification is fixed before the run: two forms of s_i (source-mean logit and rank-2 low-rank/IRT difficulty), with or without p̂^CF, and ridge or no ridge. The whole grid is reported, and one variant is chosen by the leave-one-benchmark-out rule. It is also reported in the interpolation and lineage splits, and one cell that did not motivate the design is flagged as the clean test.
- **Closest comparator:** the contrast that decides whether 3b adds anything is stratified × 3b with s_i = source difficulty, against stratified × Hájek and uniform × 3b. If 3b adds nothing over stratify-and-post-stratify, the paper reports that.
- **Lineage:** 3b is stated as the model-assisted regression (GREG) estimator (Särndal et al.) and PPI++ with a fitted slope. The new part is the application and the extrapolation analysis. `prior_work.md` says the same.
- **Small-n rule:** fitted values are clipped to [0,1] and the fit is ridge-penalised. It falls back to the Hájek sample mean if either class has fewer than 3 sampled items or the fit is rank-deficient. The fall-back rate is reported by n and split.

I sent the same specification to analysis in `experiment-repo`#6. Its results have not come back yet.
